# reac-pw / fuzz_rate

reac-pw's own fuzz target `fuzz_rate` ([source](source/fuzz_rate.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over reac-pw 1.0.42 (FreeREAC/reac-pw at f86a30a3).

Builds a PipeWire Props object from the input and parses its sample-rate key; then decides the parsed rate and a second input rate for a master or slave with a fuzz-chosen drivable mask, and writes the drivable-rate list into a fuzz-sized buffer, comparing each answer with the closed rate list and the record of the object written. The key and the refusal enumeration come from libreac's configuration header; the harness works out each rate's bit from its own closed list and names each refusal code itself.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static library of reac-pw's nine input readers and the harness's box-model table, built from source with libreac's and PipeWire SPA's headers only; neither library is linked.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- A Props write with no rate key returns 0 and leaves the caller's rate unchanged ([lines 130-141](source/fuzz_rate.c#L130-L141)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A rate key holding an Int, or a Float whose nearest integer fits an int, returns 1 and that rate (the first such key's) ([lines 143-156](source/fuzz_rate.c#L143-L156)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A rate key with no usable number, or an object that is not a Props object, returns -1 and leaves the caller's rate unchanged ([lines 158-173](source/fuzz_rate.c#L158-L173)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The decision refuses a slave first, then a rate off the closed list (44100, 48000, 96000), then a rate outside the drivable mask, and accepts every other rate ([lines 175-188](source/fuzz_rate.c#L175-L188)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Each refusal publishes its own code from the shared vocabulary ([lines 190-200](source/fuzz_rate.c#L190-L200)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A rate's bit is its place in the closed list, it is in the list exactly when it has a bit, and the best drivable rate is the highest one in the mask ([lines 202-215](source/fuzz_rate.c#L202-L215)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The drivable list is the drivable rates in ascending order, comma separated; the length returned is the whole list's and the buffer holds as much as fits, NUL-terminated ([lines 217-229](source/fuzz_rate.c#L217-L229)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch reac-pw` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz_rate.plain` | 53,632 | `2bbd88d40188265153dbe7205abefd9dcdf66369c9cb99e8588999d081a221e6` |
| ubsan | `fuzz_rate.ubsan` | 54,736 | `75532555040f82db14128f76fd4d2d19936b993e04ec7c7621cdc5e521e161e8` |
| asan | `fuzz_rate.asan` | 584,568 | `22bc8613d780c9a99353dc86368f9401311ef5c8358882651217836298529b6a` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzz_rate.asan-ubsan` | 585,336 | `c30584a7214902c43e35abebe35194418b7fdefacb6e7ed16fe0492228ec1d14` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
